bullets.title: Nasdaq 100 rips 2.5%+ to June highs; ARKK at YTD high; upside vol > downside vol
bullets.body: The QQQ gained over 2.5% intraday, returning the NASDAQ to June 1st price levels for the first time. ARKK hit YTD highs trading above its 200-day MA by the widest margin since December. A notably different tape character: upside volatility in Nasdaq is now running hotter than downside, with NDX November skew repricing sharply from Friday. SPX 7475 had a large 20k 0DTE call position to watch for gamma pinning.

bullets.title: AMD crosses $1T market cap milestone; CPU/chip complex surges on agentic AI demand
bullets.body: AMD hit $1 trillion market cap for the first time and reached new all-time highs, with shares up ~9%+. The broader CPU complex ripped: INTC +14%, ARM +14%, MU +2%, AAOI +3.4%. The thesis is agentic AI shifting the GPU-to-CPU ratio from ~7:1 (training) toward 3:1 or lower (inference), with consumer agent adoption (Meta Muse, Grok) likely underestimated in current forecasts. INTC was specifically cited as a Muse CPU demand beneficiary, with NVIDIA selecting Intel Xeon 6 as host CPU for DGX Rubin NVL8.

bullets.title: META surges 10%+ on Muse AI agent launch; Shopify partners with Muse for agentic checkout
bullets.body: META extended gains to ~10.4%, breaking above its 200-day MA by the widest margin in 12 months, after CEO Tobi Lütke of Shopify confirmed a Muse partnership enabling AI-powered agentic checkout via Shop Pay across all Shopify stores. Muse clocked 1.8M downloads and 642k DAU in its first 12 days vs ChatGPT's 1.3M downloads and 231k DAU. META's revenue per employee has doubled to $2.9M from $1.4M in early 2023 on flat headcount. Analysis flagged Meta's new subsea 'Petal' cable (petabit capacity, first transoceanic at that scale) and Muse's ability to capture purchase-intent signals to compete for ad revenue historically dominated by Google.

bullets.title: Amazon blocks Meta's Muse agent from its retail site; agentic commerce battle lines drawn
bullets.body: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from accessing its online shopping platform per Bloomberg, signaling a competitive standoff over who controls the AI-agent commerce layer. Analysts note Amazon faces difficulty distinguishing AI buyers from human buyers via existing IP/cookie methods, and that Amazon is unlikely to develop a dominant personal AI assistant—leaving Meta well-positioned as the shopping agent entry point. The conflict frames AMZN vs META as the central agentic commerce rivalry.

bullets.title: US-China trade truce extension proposed; Trump-Xi meeting imminent; Bessent touts 'deliverables'
bullets.body: The US proposed extending the China trade truce by six months while China pushed for a longer extension. Treasury Secretary Bessent said US-China talks yielded 'deliverables' covering tariffs, economics, and AI, and signaled Trump and Xi could meet two more times after this week. A formal AI 'incident line' is planned with a US-China AI meeting in Shenzhen within two months. Fox Business reported Trump will decide on a US-China AI deal this week.

bullets.title: Bessent: rates should fall post-Iran conflict; bonds unusually correlated with energy
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent said interest rates should decline once the Iran conflict resolves and repeatedly noted an unusual correlation between bonds and energy prices. He also flagged that the 30-year yield has not risen much despite buyback expansion, that he raised the Treasury buyback size during an illiquid period, and that AI labs need to take responsibility for themselves rather than rely on government oversight.

bullets.title: Diesel hits record $6.51/gal; Russia extends export ban; fuel crisis pressures inflation
bullets.body: US diesel prices surged to an all-time high above $6.51/gallon, up ~76% year-over-year and ~18% from the August average, while Russia is set to extend its diesel export ban beyond September amid continued Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries (Moscow's Gazprom Neft refinery halted Sunday). Chevron's CEO warned supply buffers have worn thin. Surging fuel costs could push US inflation expectations higher; Michigan sentiment data due Friday may not yet fully capture the spike. Republican lawmakers are exploring a diesel export ban and gas-tax holiday.

bullets.title: Oil drops 2-4% as Saudi flows defy Hormuz disruption; diplomacy hopes ease shortage fears
bullets.body: Brent fell ~2.6% to $101 and WTI dropped below $98 as Saudi Aramco loaded 14 million barrels on seven VLCCs, with shipments through Hormuz averaging 2.9 million bpd vs 700,000 in August. Diplomatic optimism around US-China and Iran talks further eased shortage fears despite a tanker struck by projectile debris in Hormuz and Libya's Sharara pipeline shutdown. US SPR crude stocks fell to 284.6M barrels, the lowest since 1982. Brent briefly fell below $100 for the first time since September 9.

bullets.title: Trump signals pro-AI, light-touch regulatory stance; no liability shield for AI labs
bullets.body: Trump posted 'Whoever wins AI, WINS,' called AI potentially bigger than the Industrial Revolution and internet, and pledged not to stifle AI growth—while Bessent noted AI labs must self-regulate and the Trump admin will not grant a liability shield to AI companies. Trump said the DOJ may regulate AI 'if we have to' but prefers current law enforcement as sufficient. Bessent also floated an 'AI czar' role to establish guardrails around incidents.

bullets.title: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee: rate-hike cycle near limit; further tightening 'necessarily painful'
bullets.body: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee indicated the central bank has reached the limit of its rate-hiking cycle, describing further tightening as 'necessarily painful,' and clarified he does not view potential rate hikes as rolling back 2025 cuts. He also warned Fed rate projections may be insufficient if inflation remains demand-driven rather than supply-constrained.

bullets.title: Bank of Canada: new era of uncertainty persists; Q4 growth could halve if US tariffs hold
bullets.body: BoC Governor Macklem warned of a prolonged era of uncertainty and said Q4 Canadian growth could be roughly halved if new US tariffs remain in place. He noted energy price pressures risk adding persistence to headline inflation, and warned that moving too slowly on rate hikes creates the risk of needing to raise rates sharply later.

bullets.title: Market breadth weakening: <30% of S&P stocks above 50-day MA; A/D line at 200-day
bullets.body: Goldman noted less than 30% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average, signaling broad market weakness beneath the index resilience. The S&P 500 advance-decline line is trending down and sitting on its 200-day MA. SPX/NDX volatility spread returned to long-term mean after July's divergence where Nasdaq fell 8% while S&P fell 3%, partly due to oil and rates exposure in the S&P's sector mix. Goldman also called gold 'particularly interesting' with Bernstein cutting its 2030 target to $5,600/oz from $6,100.

bullets.title: SoftBank selling $11B junk bonds at record yields to fund OpenAI investment
bullets.body: SoftBank plans to raise $11 billion via junk bond issuance at soaring yields to fund its OpenAI investments, with the bonds hitting record high yields. Apollo separately warned the entire hyperscaler credit story rests on the consensus assumption that operating cash flow grows 3x from $600B to $2T; a miss would trigger wider credit spreads and potential capex cuts.

bullets.title: FAA grounds all major NY-area airports on equipment/communications outage
bullets.body: The FAA issued ground stops at Newark, Philadelphia, JFK, LaGuardia, and Boston due to a loss-of-communications issue at the Philadelphia facility—the same facility responsible for prior Newark disruptions. A new circuit was readied for installation with expected resolution by ~1:30 PM local time, though New York ground stop timelines remained unclear.

bullets.title: Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger clears antitrust hurdle with state AG settlement
bullets.body: A coalition of state AGs settled their antitrust lawsuit against the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger. Key terms include WBD committing at least $1.5B to domestic film production over five years, minimum theatrical release commitments, $300M+ incremental US production spend, a $47.5M five-year commitment, editorial independence boards for CNN and CBS, and a compliance monitor overseen by a committee of five states.

bullets.title: China's CXMT enters mass production with next-gen DRAM; memory supply dynamics shifting
bullets.body: China's CXMT launched its G5 DRAM platform into mass production with 50% higher die-per-wafer density using SAQP to achieve 11.95nm half-pitch, approaching world-leading specifications. A separate SK Hynix packaging executive signaled there 'isn't much time left to survive on memory,' implying acute pressure on traditional memory business models from the HBM transition.

bullets.title: Grok 4.7 launches: competitive AI model at $2/$6 per M tokens with coding/agentic gains
bullets.body: xAI released Grok 4.7, described as a notable improvement over 4.6 at the same price and speed, priced at $2/M input and $6/M output tokens. Third-party benchmarks rank it third for agentic coding behind Anthropic and OpenAI. NVIDIA's accelerated computing infrastructure supports Grok 4.7. OpenAI is reportedly developing features specifically to counter Grok bot, signaling the AI model arms race is intensifying.

bullets.title: Google clarifies Gemini 4 uses TPUs not NVIDIA GPUs; training stack remains JAX/XLA
bullets.body: A clarification circulated that Gemini 4 was not trained on NVIDIA GB GPUs and continues to use Google's TPU stack with JAX/XLA/Pathways. Separately, NVIDIA's Vera CPUs posted 48% faster database query performance than Intel Xeon 6 with fewer cores, while an Intel executive confirmed the CPU shortage is real, with competition among INTC, AMD, and AMZN's Graviton in data center applications.

bullets.title: French sovereign risk rising: CDS at 45bps (highest since March 2020); debt to near 120% GDP
bullets.body: French 5-year CDS spreads hit 45 basis points, the highest since March 2020, as the French finance ministry forecast record government debt approaching 120% of GDP in 2026. This represents a widening European sovereign risk signal worth monitoring for cross-asset spillover into US credit and rates.

bullets.title: Trump-Greenland signing ceremony Tuesday; Boeing 200 China aircraft orders progressing
bullets.body: The US, Denmark, and Greenland will hold a signing ceremony Tuesday per Fox, as Denmark confirmed the deal would boost Arctic security. Separately, USTR Ambassador Greer confirmed Boeing is making progress on finalizing 200 Chinese airplane orders announced earlier this year, a rare positive signal on US-China trade deliverables.
